concepts.label: cbepctl
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing concept anywhere in the registry or extraction layer, despite cbepctl-intro.md and a large family of cbepctl subcommand pages existing in the source tree; none had apparently crossed the recurrence bar before this round. The ep-engine/memcached control tool this 'set checkpoint_param' subcommand belongs to.

concepts.label: vBucket checkpoint
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already minted elsewhere as the per-vBucket data structure cbstats exposes; this page is the configuration-side counterpart, letting an administrator tune checkpoint sizing and destruction via cbepctl rather than merely reading checkpoint state via cbstats.

concepts.label: Bucket memory quota
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already minted elsewhere; this page's checkpoint_memory_ratio parameter caps checkpoint memory as a fraction of this quota.

relations.subject: tool:cbepctl
relations.evidence: This command changes checkpoint configuration parameters.

relations.subject: vbucket:checkpoint
relations.evidence: checkpoint\_memory\_ratio                 | Maximum portion of the bucket quota that the system can allocate to checkpoints.

notable_absence.finding: This page's Syntax line - 'cbepctl [host]:11210 -b [bucket-name] set checkpoint_param [parameter] [value]' - shows no -u/-p credential flags at all, and the page never names an RBAC role. Its sibling page in this same batch, set-flush_param.md, DOES show '-u [administrator-name] -p [administrator-password]' explicitly in its own Syntax line for the same tool. That is a real, page-to-page inconsistency within one cbepctl subcommand family, not merely an absence - either this page omits credentials cbepctl actually requires, or the two subcommands genuinely differ in what they need, and neither possibility is explained. A clean example of the lighter, per-subcommand-page authorship this round is watching for.

cross_component_finding: This is the first page in the corpus to configure vbucket:checkpoint rather than merely read it (cbstats exposes checkpoint state; cbepctl's set checkpoint_param subcommand changes it). The registry's own vbucket:checkpoint note already anticipates a page like this one, explicitly distinguishing the ep-engine/KV checkpoint documented here from xdcr:checkpoint-document's unrelated, XDCR-replication-specific checkpoint mechanism - this page confirms that distinction holds: nothing here concerns XDCR at all, despite the shared word 'checkpoint'.
cross_product_finding: No Capella content; cbepctl is a low-level ep-engine control tool operating directly against a node's memcached port (11210), a level of access Capella does not expose to customers.
